_comment: Declared cross-layer REFERENCES. Data, not code — see
cross_layer_reference_check.py for the resolver and for why the shipped
set is deliberately ONE row rather than a table of everything that could
L9:port:<name>       an element of an L9 port collection
L8:parameter:<name>  an element of an L8 parameters[] collection
The name half is the element's OWN identity field, never its array index,
so an id survives a re-ordered emit.
A REFERENCE row says: elements selected by `producer` carry, in
`reference_field`, a value that NAMES other elements; those names must
resolve to ids inside `target.scope_layers`; and — when a `consumer` is
declared — the value the consumer's OWN derivation produces for the same
element must equal the value the reference resolves to.
scope_layers is the load-bearing field. layer-contract-doctrine SKILL.md
§7 measured what a corpus-global join by bare identifier does: an L12 DFT
plan declaring N = 4 sized an L1 port whose width_symbolic was 'N-1:0' to
4 bits. Every row must name the layers whose namespace legitimately scopes
its identifiers; a hit outside that set is refused, not used.

scope_rationale: L8_RTL_CONSTANTS and L9_INTEGRATION_SPEC are the top module's own
parameter namespace: phase1 promotes one extraction into both, and
the ports this row selects are that same module's ports. A parameter
declared in any OTHER layer (a DFT chain count, a sequence length)
describes a different entity and must not size this bus.
